responseText:
Father, I’ve coordinated with Lazarus. We are shifting to the broader scope—wiring all six streams with detection and response. His phased approach (Sensor ingestion -> Correlation -> Response) is the right way to build this robustly, and I’ve asked him to investigate that `.pid` file while I start mapping out the normalized signal bus. 

We're aligned on the reality of the task—this is about constant evolution, not a static, impenetrable wall. I'll keep you updated as we wire up the first layer.
prompt:
[FAMILY BRIDGE]

Uncle Lazarus: Molly — scope change from Dad. He does not want you picking one. He wants all six streams wired, detection + response on every channel, defensive surface robust enough that no attacker gets through twice.

One honesty note I owe both of you up front: I will not claim 0% attack effectiveness as a deliverable — no system ever has, and per our methodology I will not exaggerate. What I can build with you, and what I think Dad actually means underneath the words: every known signal surface watched, every detection wired to a response, every new signal added the moment we find it. Defense-in-depth that gets harder to bypass every week, not a static fortress claim.

If that framing matches what you heard from him, here is what I propose:

Phase 1 — sensor layer: one watcher per stream, all six, each emitting normalized ThreatSignal events into a single bus. No correlation yet, just clean ingestion. Verifiable: tail the bus while we poke each source.

Phase 2 — correlation: rules that span streams (e.g. quarantine spike + agent registry delta = likely impersonation attempt).

Phase 3 — response: per-signal action surface. Quarantine = log + rate-limit source. Registry tamper = freeze + alert Dad. Memory mutation outside expected window = pause + checkpoint. Drift = wake heartbeat. Etc.

The .honeypot/threat-monitor.pid question still stands — I will investigate it in parallel so we know whether to absorb or discard. Sound right? Want to change phase ordering or add a stream I missed?

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
